Anna L.: Running into TS inference break in ESM edge functions (Vercel). SDK compile errors: "No overload expects 1 arguments" and "Type parameter T could not be inferred" when calling client.generate.

Mike T.: Can you share a minimal repro and tsconfig?

Anna L.: Minimal repro: imports from @redwood/inference in an ESM file with moduleResolution=nodenext. Runtime OK, tsc fails.

Sophia R.: Known pattern: nodenext changes how TypeScript resolves package exports and d.ts. If TS picks the CJS entrypoint, overloaded signatures can mismatch and break inference.

Mike T.: Short-term: explicit generic (client.generate<MyShape>(...)) or suggest moduleResolution=nodenext in docs. Long term: ensure package.json exports map points ESM imports to the ESM build and include a proper "types" field so tsc picks correct declarations.

Sophia R.: Also ergonomic fix: add an overload that defaults generics to any for inference-friendly quickstarts, while keeping strict generic overloads for explicit typing. Example: overload with GenerateOpts<any> then generic GenerateOpts<T>.

ci-bot: Created PR to add exports alias and types field (CI pending).

Anna L.: Thanks. Can we add a short FAQ for Edge TypeScript settings in the SDK README and update sample-apps templates to show explicit generic usage? That will reduce onboarding friction.

Mike T.: I'll update sample-apps and run Vercel/Cloudflare templates once the PR lands.

Sophia R.: Will push package.json + d.ts build fixes and add a compile-only test for nodenext fixtures.
